messages.subject: Re: How to call function that calls function that makes ggplot2 charts?
parts:
This very simple example works. I imagine yours is more complex though. 



funcplot <- function(x) {
  qplot(x[,1], x[,2], data = x, geom="point")
}
funcplot(data.frame(rnorm(20), rnorm(20)))

funcplot2 <- function(y) {
  z <- y
  funcplot(z)  
}
funcplot2(data.frame(rnorm(20), rnorm(20)))


Scott

messages.subject: Re: How to call function that calls function that makes ggplot2 charts?
parts:
I think the problem is that you are referring to the variables within the aes call incorrectly. Instead refer to the name of the column itself without the data frame name included. 


df <- data.frame(var1=rnorm(20), var2=rnorm(20))

funcplot <- function(x) {
  ggplot(x, aes(x=var1, y=var2)) + geom_point()
}

funcplot(df)



Scott

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: How to call function that calls function that makes ggplot2 charts?
parts: Use aes_string. The issue is that aes expects a unqouted var name. names returns a quoted character string.

df <- data.frame(var1=rnorm(20), var2=rnorm(20))

funcplot <- function(x) {

ggplot(x, aes_string(x = names(x)[1], y = names(x)[2])) + geom_point()
}

funcplot(df)
Luciano

messages.subject: Re: How to call function that calls function that makes ggplot2 charts?
parts:
Scott,

I cannot refer to the columns by name because I don't really know
their names. I've just tried rewriting funcplot using aes_string as
follows ... and it worked.

funcplot <- function(x) {
ggplot(x, aes_string(x=names(x)[1], y=names(x)[2])) + geom_point()
}

However, my function, which I think is just to long to post here still
didn't work after making analogous change. It uses a variable to
store the chart, so a more faithful analogy would be:

funcplot <- function(x) {
chart <- ggplot(x, aes_string(x=names(x)[1], y=names(x)[2])) +
geom_point()
chart
}

On a hunch, I added a 'print' statement to display the variable
storing the chart at the end of the function ... the structure below
worked perfectly ... but I don't know why.

funcplot <- function(x) {
chart <- ggplot(x, aes_string(x=names(x)[1], y=names(x)[2])) +
geom_point()
print(chart)
chart
}

Thanks for your help
